Yu Liu 刘宇

Mathematics / Scientific Computing / Backend Development

I hold an M.Phil. in Mathematics from The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, and a B.Sc. in Mathematics and Applied Mathematics from Tongji University. My research interests are numerical analysis, scientific computing, and numerical methods for stochastic differential equations.

My master's research focused on Monte Carlo valuation and trading strategies for Chinese convertible bonds. I subsequently worked in backend development at BYD and Xiaoniu Hulian, contributing to content-management systems and AI application backends.

I am currently strengthening my background in stochastic analysis, including Brownian motion, Itô integration, and Itô's formula, with an interest in approximation and error analysis for numerical methods for stochastic differential equations.

I am applying for Ph.D. programs in applied mathematics and scientific computing for Fall 2027.

Research

Valuation Model of Chinese Convertible Bonds Based on Monte Carlo Simulation: A Regression-Based Approximation and Error Analysis

Yu Liu · arXiv:2409.06496 · 2024, revised 2026

A regression-based Monte Carlo method for Chinese convertible bonds with path-dependent call and put triggers. The method combines least-squares continuation-value estimation with backward dynamic programming, compares global and price-region regressions, and examines convergence and approximation error.

Preprint; not peer-reviewed. A smaller one-step population projection error does not guarantee a smaller finite-sample pricing error.

Paper PDFarXivMaster's thesis

Wavelet-Based Image Restoration

Undergraduate thesis · Tongji University · Advisor: Jae Kyu Choi

Studied analysis-based, synthesis-based, and balanced wavelet-frame formulations for image reconstruction, and an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) approach to the analysis-based formulation.

Convertible-Bond Ranking and Simulated Trading

Compared linear regression, SVM, random forests, XGBoost, LightGBM, and MLP models using rolling-window train–test splits. Evaluated factors through information coefficient (IC) analysis and stratified backtesting, and explored automated simulated trading. The ranking page is updated on a schedule using GitHub Actions.
